examTakeaway: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is a deficiency of ADAMTS13, so huge von Willebrand multimers make platelet thrombi. Platelet transfusion is not the treatment of the count.
scenario: A 35-year-old man has platelets of 15,000, schistocytes, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, and confusion. Coagulation times are normal. A classmate orders platelets to 50,000 as the only therapy. He is the patient in front of the clinician.
question: Which protein is missing, and why are platelets alone the wrong plan?
options: Factor VIII is missing, so platelets are the replacement
Spectrin is missing, so splenectomy tonight is the only care
ADAMTS13 is high, so more platelets are required to match it
Immunoglobulin against glycoproteins, treated only by transfusion
ADAMTS13 is missing. Plasma exchange, not platelet transfusion, is the disease treatment
correctAnswer: ADAMTS13 is missing. Plasma exchange, not platelet transfusion, is the disease treatment
explanation:
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is a deficiency of ADAMTS13, so huge von Willebrand multimers make platelet thrombi. Platelet transfusion is not the treatment of the count. Normal coagulation times separate this from disseminated intravascular coagulation. Transfusing platelets can feed the thrombi. ISTH guidance on thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, 2020.

ADAMTS13 is missing. Plasma exchange, not platelet transfusion, is the disease treatment
Factor VIII is missing, so platelets are the replacement — Coagulation times would be abnormal in a factor deficiency of that size, and the smear would not show schistocytes as the main clue.
Spectrin is missing, so splenectomy tonight is the only care — Spherocytes, not schistocytes and confusion, mark that disease.
ADAMTS13 is high, so more platelets are required to match it — The enzyme is deficient, not high.
Immunoglobulin against glycoproteins, treated only by transfusion — That is immune thrombocytopenia, which lacks schistocytes and organ failure.
citation: ISTH guidance on thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, 2020.
